name: Roland JUPITER-X/Xm
description: Roland JUPITER-X and JUPITER-Xm ZEN-Core synthesizers: the temporary scene (common, five parts with their zones, EQs, MFX and arpeggios, chorus, delay, reverb, drive) and part 1's temporary tone in each of its four kinds — Z-Core (four partials with envelopes, LFOs, EQ and the synth layer), Analog Synth Model, RD Piano and the JUPITER-X model — with the system settings.

sources.title: JUPITER-X/Xm MIDI Implementation (version 1.06, Apr 19, 2022)
sources.notes: Parameter Address Map read by tools/profiles/roland/parse-address-map.mjs from JUPITER-X_Xm_MIDI_imple_eng06_W.pdf (sha256 426dedfcea5fd6957af38ecc9fb5b1813fdc124fb0d95d950ebc6ee342f6127b). Model ID 00 00 00 65, DT1 = 12, RQ1 = 11, Roland checksum. Not yet checked against the instrument itself.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/roland/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/roland/synths/, not this file.
Every parameter is the manual's, at the manual's address, with the manual's name. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

Part 1's tones: Z-Core at 02 00 00 00, Analog Synth Model at 02 10 00 00, RD Piano at 02 20 00 00, JUPITER-X model at 02 50 00 00. A part plays one kind at a time; Scene Part Tone Bank Select / Program Change say which.
Rows marked (*) are not used with the JUPITER-Xm (the manual's footnote); their ids leave the mark out, their names keep it.

Tone Partial DelayTime (note) (p80) carries the manual's labels as printed: "1/64T, 1/8, 1/64, 1/32T, …, 1/16., 1/4T, …". The JUNO-X manual prints the same row with 1/8 tenth (after 1/16.), the order of note lengths; if that is right, values 1-9 here are labelled one place off.

Rows the manual prints more than once in a block under one unnumbered name (the two LFOs and their sixteen Steps and Step Curves in Partial LFO, the four partials' rows in the PMTs, the four Matrix Control sets in Tone Partial, MFX CtrlAsgn, a tone's Name bytes) keep the manual's name; the generator tells them apart by address, as <id>_<last two address bytes>.
Scene Delay and System Delay are laid out with the [Chorus] table, which is what the map links them to (there is no [Delay] table), so their rows are named "Chorus …"; the ids drop the word.
Part 5 is the rhythm part (PART R in the manual's own labels). Its tone is a drum kit (Bank Select MSB 86), and the address map has no temporary drum-kit area, so nothing of a kit is here.

Grid Offset, Offset Velocity and Probability Grid Offset (Arpeggio Part), Mic Noise Suppressor Threshold (System Common) and AMP MOD (Analog Synth Model) are two-nibble values whose printed wire range starts below zero; the engine cannot send a negative value, and how the instrument encodes one (two's complement, presumably) is not printed.

Not read at startup (read on request, since the instrument may not answer them): part1.zcore.common, part1.zcore.mfx, part1.zcore.pmt, part1.zcore.partial1, part1.zcore.partial1.pitchEnv, part1.zcore.partial1.filterEnv, part1.zcore.partial1.ampEnv, part1.zcore.partial1.lfo, part1.zcore.partial1.eq, part1.zcore.partial1.synth, part1.zcore.partial2, part1.zcore.partial2.pitchEnv, part1.zcore.partial2.filterEnv, part1.zcore.partial2.ampEnv, part1.zcore.partial2.lfo, part1.zcore.partial2.eq, part1.zcore.partial2.synth, part1.zcore.partial3, part1.zcore.partial3.pitchEnv, part1.zcore.partial3.filterEnv, part1.zcore.partial3.ampEnv, part1.zcore.partial3.lfo, part1.zcore.partial3.eq, part1.zcore.partial3.synth, part1.zcore.partial4, part1.zcore.partial4.pitchEnv, part1.zcore.partial4.filterEnv, part1.zcore.partial4.ampEnv, part1.zcore.partial4.lfo, part1.zcore.partial4.eq, part1.zcore.partial4.synth, part1.zcore.synth, part1.zcore.synthPmt, part1.analog, part1.analog.mfx, part1.analog.common, rdPiano, rdPiano.resonance, part1.jupiterX, part1.jupiterX.mfx, part1.jupiterX.common.

coverage.inboundControllers: not modelled: the front panel's CCs are in the Control Change section, not the address map
coverage.effectParameterMeanings: type-dependent: MFX, chorus, delay and reverb parameters are Roland's 4-nibble container (12768-52768, shown -20000..+20000); what each slot does depends on the selected type, which the MIDI Implementation does not list
coverage.names: not text: the manual prints each name byte as its own row ("Name" sixteen times in a tone, "NAME 1"-"NAME 16" in the scene), which the generator's name reader does not join, so a name is sixteen 32-127 (ASCII) parameters
coverage.tones: part 1 only. Left out: parts 2-4's Z-Core tones (02 01 00 00, 02 02 00 00, 02 03 00 00), Analog Synth Model tones (02 11 00 00, 02 12 00 00, 02 13 00 00) and JUPITER-X model tones (02 51 00 00, 02 52 00 00, 02 53 00 00), each laid out as part 1's; the RD Piano(01) at 02 20 00 00 is the only one there is
coverage.drumKit: none: part 5 (PART R) plays a drum kit (Bank Select MSB 86, p1), and the address map has no temporary drum-kit area
coverage.userData: left out: Scene Arpeggio User Pattern (01)-(05) at 01 00 5A 00, 01 00 7A 00, 01 01 1A 00, 01 01 3A 00, 01 01 5A 00 (1,056 rows each, 2,112 bytes), User Scene (001)-(256) from 40 00 00 00 and (257)-(512) from 60 00 00 00, User Tone (001)-(512) from 50 00 00 00
coverage.systemPresets: left out: Model Bank (01)-(16) Assign at 00 00 07 00-00 00 16 00 and Button Color Set(01)-(10) at 00 00 17 00-00 00 20 00, the panel's bank-button and LED-colour settings
coverage.blockReadBack: the JUPITER-X model parameter block (part1.jupiterX, 02 50 00 00) is 269 bytes (p83); the instrument sends more than 256 bytes as packets of at most 256 (p7), and its dump here expects one message, so reading that block back is unproven. Writing its parameters is unaffected
